subject: Career
title: Using Precise Numbers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Using Precise Numbers usable.

hook.text: Asking for $103,500 is more effective than asking for $100,000. Precision signals preparation.

buildup.text: Columbia research found precise numbers are perceived as more informed and harder to counter.

discovery.text: Round numbers feel arbitrary. Precise numbers feel calculated — like they're backed by data.

twist.text: The trick works both ways. If someone offers you $100K flat, they likely haven't done deep analysis.

climax.text: Prepare your precise number before the conversation. Derive it from market data, not guesswork.

punchline.text: Precise numbers win because they look researched.

quiz.question: Why are precise salary numbers more effective than round ones?
options: They signal research and are harder to counter

details.summary: Research from Columbia Business School shows that precise salary figures such as $73,500 rather than $70,000 are perceived as more informed and yield better outcomes. Precise numbers imply you have done thorough homework and know your exact market value.
details.whyItMatters: Round numbers signal estimation; precise numbers signal research. Employers are less likely to counter-offer aggressively against figures that appear data-backed.
takeaways: Precise figures outperform round numbers in negotiations
Specificity implies thorough research and market awareness
Pair precise numbers with data sources for maximum impact

faq.question: How precise should a salary request actually be?
faq.answer: Quoting to the nearest five hundred dollars is typically sufficient. For example, asking for $87,500 instead of $90,000 signals specificity without appearing unnecessarily granular or difficult to process.

faq.question: Does this precision strategy work for hourly or freelance rates?
faq.answer: Yes. Quoting $127 per hour rather than $125 per hour triggers the same psychological effect. Clients perceive the precise figure as calculated from real project experience rather than an arbitrary round number.
